title: Molecular Gas and Star Formation in Dwarf Galaxies Observed by the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array
question: Do dwarf galaxies follow the molecular star formation law of massive spirals, and is their star formation regulated by gravitational stability (Toomre Q)?

data.sensitivity: channel rms 38-72 mK at 2 km/s resolution

what.value: Rotation velocities V_rot used for kappa

evidence.quote: $V_{\rm rot}$ is the rotational velocity obtained from (cite: 2022MNRAS.512.1012C)
(cite: Leroy_2019) convolved both sets of images to a common Gaussian PSF of 7.5$''$

recipe.method: ALMA scripts calibration, TCLEAN imaging, IMPBCOR, 3 sigma masking on 6'' smoothed map
Convolve CO cubes and 3.6um images to 7.5'' Gaussian PSF
Sigma_H2 from I_CO; Sigma_SFR from NUV+12um; Sigma_star from 3.4/3.6um
Concentric elliptical annuli of 7.5'' width; error bars are standard deviation in annulus
Least-squares power-law fit of Sigma_SFR vs Sigma_H2 per galaxy; SFE = Sigma_SFR/Sigma_H2
Two-component thick-disk Q from gas and stars
assumptions: Q_g from H2 only; sigma_z/sigma_r = 0.6 stars, 1 gas

answer_key.quantity: Mean molecular SFL slope, all six

evidence.quote: The resulting power-law indices range from 0.62 to 1.08, with a mean slope of N = 0.81$\pm$0.18.

answer_key.quantity: Mean slope, four galaxies with 3+ points

evidence.quote: yields a mean slope of N = 0.87$\pm$0.05
yielding an average index of N$=0.73\pm 0.05$
the SFE$_{\rm H_2}$ values range from 0.9 Gyr$^{-1}$ to 4.1 Gyr$^{-1}$
The $Q_{\rm tot}$ values range from 0.9 to 1.5
